hypothesis: Reading the shared input repeatedly may incur cross-adapter cache/coherency penalties. One auxiliary-GPU copy into an ordinary DEFAULT buffer might reduce the subsequent postprocessing cost enough to offset that copy.

motivation.observed_shared_input_screening: At 1080p scene100/post4, copy-path single rate 646.9225 versus dual rate 97.7157 tasks/s; direct-path single 646.1573 versus dual 101.0604. The copy-path auxiliary stage took approximately 8-9 ms versus approximately 0.155 ms on the discrete GPU, under the recorded background load.
motivation.qualification: UHD630 is UMA: an ordinary DEFAULT allocation is not new dedicated VRAM. Copying may be slower, and the current data do not prove cache behavior is the root cause.

implementation_constraint: Add orthogonal --secondary-input shared|local, default shared. Do not change shader, pixel tolerance, workload, single-GPU baseline, timestamp frequency handling, success gates, fences or three-slot ownership. Both primary transfer modes remain available.
cost_accounting: For local input, place the existing auxiliary start timestamp before shared-to-local CopyBufferRegion. Include copy, barriers and unchanged Post in post_gpu_ms and overall completion/wall rates. Read back the actual local input for correctness validation.
preflight: On the new attested binary, pure CPU self-tests and pixel validation of direct/local and copy/local must pass before timing.
environment: background_loaded_screening; do not terminate remote access, Codex, Pavise or user applications. All safety guards retained. No idle-machine or product-ready claim.

matrix.phase_order: ABBA / BAAB / ABBA within every invocation
matrix.choice_reason: Keep the already-defined low/high scene workloads, without searching intermediate loop counts. Use direct primary output to avoid adding a redundant primary local-to-shared copy in this follow-up. Rerun shared controls on the same new binary rather than comparing only against an older build.

decision: Judge every candidate against its single-GPU baseline, not only against the older dual-GPU implementation. Retain the original +2% average/wall, +1% low, >=2/3 paired wins, <=5% P99 regression and <=5% drift/timing gaps. A candidate needs independently confirmed quiet and real end-to-end benefit before shipping. If no candidate passes, stop this workload/parameter exploration and report the evidence; do not add a misleading acceleration switch.
